Cross-checking with Python

python-cross-check.Rmd

ouanalytics-py is a second implementation of the same calculations, written independently in Python with polars. It exists to catch mistakes: if two programs written separately in two languages agree on every number, a bug would have to be made twice.

What it checks

  • Every table. It recomputes each table compute_pool() returns and the playoff seeding, from the same inputs, and compares them with the R result (numbers within 1e-9, everything else exactly).
  • The data. It checks facts that must hold: no duplicate picks, each team’s wins plus losses equal its games, one grid row per team per day, points that match each pick and status, and seeds that run 1 to the number of teams.

How R hands over a case

R writes a case as CSV files in a fixed layout with export_pool_case() and export_seeding_case():

<case>/inputs/*.csv     what went in
<case>/outputs/*.csv    what R computed

Run it 

cd nba-over-under-2026-2027/ouanalytics-py
uv sync
uv run pytest                                  # tests, 100% coverage
uv run ouanalytics-check tests/golden/*        # the golden cases R wrote
uv run ouanalytics-check ../check-export/pool ../check-export/seeding   # today's build

The golden cases come from R: after any change to the R calculations, re-run ouanalytics/tools/make-golden.R, then the Python tests. A difference means one of the two is wrong.

In the daily build

The page build writes check-export/ and the cross-check runs after the page is published. A difference does not hold back the page. It opens a GitHub issue (on the Mac mini) or fails the cross-check job (on GitHub Actions) so it gets looked at.
